appraisal_events.evidence: Françoise is admitted, only 'à de certaines conditions de grande politesse,' into the hotel staff's 'difficile amitié' (the café-owner, a chambermaid, a sommelier, a kitchen hand, a floor housekeeper), whom she now treats as 'les seules gens qui comptassent pour elle'; as a result 'nous ne pouvions plus avoir d'eau chaude parce que Françoise était devenue l'amie de celui qui la faisait chauffer.'
appraisal_events.explanation: Françoise visibly crosses from having no connections at the hotel into a bounded, conditionally-entered circle of staff loyalty, and that new belonging directly reverses whose interests she serves, at the expense of the grandmother's and narrator's everyday comfort.

appraisal_events.evidence: M. de Stermaria treats meeting 'une personnalité importante' as complete in itself, needing only 'une poignée de mains et un coup d'œil pénétrant sans conversation immédiate ni relations ultérieures,' and returns to his seat 'en se frottant les mains comme un homme qui vient de faire une précieuse acquisition.'
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's ironic description of his satisfied hand-rubbing over a merely symbolic handshake exposes M. de Stermaria's status-seeking as shallow and self-congratulatory.

status_effects.explanation: She is shown crossing from no relations at the hotel into the staff's exclusive, conditionally-guarded circle of mutual friendship.
Her new staff loyalties give her the leverage to withhold small services from her own employers without consequence, reversing who controls whom day to day.
She loses the practical deference she is paying for, unable even to get hot water when cold, because Françoise now answers to her staff friends first.
Like his grandmother, he finds himself unable to summon basic service from Françoise, who now prioritizes her hotel-staff friendships.
The narrator's ironic framing of his satisfaction with an empty social gesture exposes him as shallow and status-hungry.
